correctness.rationale: Three perfect matchings contain a total of |E| edge slots, so a cover partitions the edges. Labelling the three nonempty colour classes gives a free six-element action. On a replacement triangle the internal edges must use all three colours, forcing the external colours to be distinct and determining each internal edge by the opposite external one. On a two-terminal unit each colour is a matching, so its number of external incidences has the parity of the unit's (even) order; the two terminal links must have the same colour. A 2-cycle then has the two orders of the other colours, and in a diamond the two orders of the side colours at one terminal each force all remaining edges. The channel rules multiply independently; in a ring the common link colour gives an extra factor of three. Both exceptional graphs have six labelled colourings. Zhou–Wang's Lemma 2.1 matches the stated connected multigraph scope and (1) gives |V(G)|=3|V(H)|+4ℓ+2r, with totals ℓ,r. The small-core fact can be checked without relying on the book census: in a minimum non-3-edge-colourable bridgeless loopless cubic multigraph a triangle contracts or a double edge smooths to a smaller bridgeless cubic graph with equivalent colourability (the triple edge is already colourable, and coincident external endpoints of a double edge would force a bridge). A perfect matching exists by Petersen's theorem. Its complementary 2-factor must contain an even positive number of odd cycles, of lengths at least five after the reductions. Thus no smaller obstruction exists and any obstruction of order ten consists of two chordless 5-cycles with a matching between them. An adjacent pair matched to an adjacent pair gives a Hamilton cycle, hence a 3-edge-colouring. Otherwise the matching identifies one cycle with the complement of the other, giving Petersen. In Petersen a perfect matching uses 1, 3 or 5 spokes: three is impossible because the two unmatched indices cannot be adjacent on both cycles, while one and five each leave odd cycles. This proves the required uniqueness, and equality at 30 forces no channel units. The frozen verify.py was inspected, not executed; its finite examples do not yield the global taxonomy or the census.

evidence: The flow theorem for bridgeless connected multigraphs contracts each connected side in turn and divides the product of the two resulting flow polynomials by the falling factorial (λ−1)_{|S|−1}. broader_coverage.reasoning: At four the denominators are 3 and 6. The hypotheses apply: the two links of a channel unit or a ring unit separate connected sides in a bridgeless graph; after unit reduction, the triangle cut has connected exterior because a connected bridgeless cubic core has no cut vertex. The initiating paper's parity lemma concerns one perfect matching, not this factorization.

evidence: Cutting off a diamond or 2-cycle and suppressing the degree-two cap vertices in the two factors gives respectively K₄ or K₂³ on the gadget side and the graph with the unit bypassed on the other. Both gadget factors have F(4)=6. Cutting off a triangle gives a K₄ factor and the triangle contraction.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Subdivision does not change flow counts. The cut formulas therefore give exactly 6/3=2 per two-terminal unit and 6/6=1 per replacement triangle. Iteration ends at H in type (iii), or at K₄/K₂³ for a one-unit ring and so gives 6·2^(q−1) labelled ring colourings. Dividing by six gives every count claimed. Zero count is then exactly zero core count. With a simple core, substituting the classical Petersen minimum and uniqueness into the nonnegative vertex-count formula yields the order-30 corollary.

evidence: On a cubic multigraph a nowhere-zero flow with values in the Klein four-group has three distinct nonzero values at each vertex, so F_G(4) equals the labelled Tait count. Dong's (2.5) factors F_G across two- and three-edge cuts.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Signs are immaterial in the Klein group and three nonzero values sum to zero exactly when all are different. Thus the flow count divided by six is the precise unordered three-cover count with the frozen parallel edges treated as distinct edges. The alias is mathematically exact.

value.rationale: Three-cover counts are a natural baseline for the four- and five-cover problems, and the decomposition gives a convenient presentation. But the exact invariant here is obtained by evaluating an existing stronger flow formula at four and substituting two elementary gadget values. The cutoff is likewise a direct order substitution and adds no new core classification. The record neither computes the hard core count in general nor establishes any independent consequence beyond these deductions.
